text_blocks.snippet: Lung hyperinflation is a condition where the lungs become overfilled with air, often due to an obstruction in the airways. This can lead to a range of symptoms and complications, including shortness of breath, and can put extra strain on the heart and other respiratory muscles.

list.title: COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease):
list.snippet: This is the most common cause, with emphysema and chronic bronchitis being major contributors.

list.title: Asthma:
list.snippet: Severe, persistent asthma can also lead to hyperinflation.

list.title: Other respiratory infections:
list.snippet: Conditions like pneumonia or bronchitis can cause inflammation and airway obstruction, contributing to hyperinflation.

list.title: Exposure to pollutants and smoke:
list.snippet: Long-term exposure to irritants like smoke or pollutants can damage the lungs and cause hyperinflation.
